title: TUR installed-application record
description: What tur-apps keeps about one application it installed: $XDG_DATA_HOME/tur/apps/installed/<id>.json. It ties the catalogue's identifier to what was installed by which route. Written by tur-apps only; read back with a 256 KiB cap; a record that names another application, or a route that does not match what it holds, is refused. See docs/architecture/app-install-backend.md.

id.description: The catalogue identifier. Also the record's file name, for a Windows application the identifier tur-runtime keeps it under, and for a re-hosted application the identifier tur-rehost keeps it under.

installed_at.description: When, in UTC, RFC 3339 to the second.

rehost.description: Absent in a record written before the re-hosted route existed; read as null.

source.description: What the application was installed from.

pinned.description: Whether the file's SHA-256 matched the one the catalogue pins. A user's file for an application with no pin is false. For a re-hosted application: whether it is the package TUR measured.

flatpak.description: What a Flatpak installation consists of.

added_refs.description: Every reference the installation added: the application, runtimes, extensions, translations. Removal takes away those no other application uses.

windows.description: What a Windows installation consists of.

rehost.description: What a re-hosted installation consists of: the person's Windows or macOS package, laid by tur-rehost under the Linux build of its own runtime.

platform.description: windows or macos, as tur-rehost reported it.

runtime.description: The runtime it runs on, such as "electron 44.10.2".

measured.description: Whether the package was the one TUR measured: its SHA-256 equals the one in the catalogue's record of TUR's test.

builds_allowed.description: Whether the person allowed native modules to be built from source on this computer.

allowed_unresolved.description: Native modules with no Linux build that tur-rehost was allowed to leave out, because TUR's measurement of this package showed that it starts without them. Empty for a package TUR did not measure.
